label: catechol degradation I (meta-cleavage pathway)
status: Recommended for next complete curation; source-intake author proposal, not final acceptance
chosen_scope: The full five-step hydrolytic catechol meta-cleavage route to formate, pyruvate and acetyl-CoA, preserving both source child modules and their explicit ordered join.
why_not_GO: GO:0019616 names meta-cleavage generally and covers hydrolytic and oxidative variants; exact native PWY-5415 preserves this route boundary. Fresh QuickGO definition and pinned GO source agree on broad wording.
taxon_limits: Native species annotations are candidate whole-route scopes, not nine newly experimentally verified route taxa. PKO1, mt-2/TOL constructs, CF600 preparations and E. coli expression hosts must remain separate; ORG-5948 lacks an NCBI xref in this original.
sibling: MetaCyc:PWY-5420 (P183-PWY replaced by four-step PWY-5419; oxidative route), retained separately and not included in proposal
shared_existing_tail: MetaCyc:PWY0-1277 contains the same PWY-5162 three-reaction terminal module but has different phenylpropanoate/hydroxyphenylpropanoate entry and ring-cleavage chemistry. Protocatechuate para-cleavage ends at the enol interface; its source references are not formal terminal membership.
source_conflict: PWY-5415 parent comment names OXOPENTENOATE (keto) and CPD-6761 (2E enol), while P183-PWY and PWY-5162 formal layouts and exact reactions connect through CPD-14447 (2Z enol). All three source structures are distinct; source-owned full structures and ChEBI exact InChI establish that distinction. Do not silently use parent narrative as chemical membership.
